246.body: Key terms and concepts used in Synapse DB documentation.
246.title: Glossary

247.body: API (Application Programming Interface) : The set of functions and methods exposed by Synapse DB for developers to interact with the database.
247.title: A

248.body: Benchmark : Performance tests that measure the speed and efficiency of database operations. Buffer : Temporary storage area in memory used for I/O operations.
248.title: B

249.body: Cache : Fast storage layer that keeps frequently accessed data in memory for quick retrieval. Cargo : Rust's package manager and build tool. Commit : A transaction operation that saves changes permanently to the database. Concurrency : The ability to handle multiple operations simultaneously. Conventional Commits : A specification for commit message format used in Synapse DB development. Crate : A Rust package or library. Synapse DB is distributed as a crate.
249.title: C

250.body: Database : An organized collection of structured data. Dependency : External library or package that Synapse DB relies on.
250.title: D

251.body: Engine : See Query Engine. Error Handling : The process of managing and responding to errors in code.
251.title: E

252.body: Git : Version control system used for Synapse DB development. GitHub Actions : CI/CD platform used to automate testing, building, and deployment.
252.title: G

253.body: Index : Data structure that improves the speed of data retrieval operations. I/O (Input/Output) : Operations that read from or write to storage.
253.title: I

254.body: Lifetime : Rust's mechanism for ensuring references are valid.
254.title: L

255.body: mdBook : Tool used to generate this documentation from Markdown files. Memory Safety : Guarantee that programs don't have undefined behavior related to memory access. MIT License : Open-source license used by Synapse DB.
255.title: M

256.body: Optimization : Process of improving query or code performance. Ownership : Rust's system for managing memory without garbage collection.
256.title: O

257.body: Parser : Component that analyzes and interprets SQL queries. Persistence : Storing data permanently to disk. Pipeline : Automated CI/CD workflow for testing and deployment.
257.title: P

258.body: Query : Request for data or information from the database. Query Engine : Component responsible for processing and executing queries. Query Optimization : Process of improving query execution performance.
258.title: Q

259.body: RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) : C++ principle adopted by Rust for automatic resource management. Rollback : Undoing changes made during a transaction. Rust : Systems programming language used to build Synapse DB. Rustfmt : Official Rust code formatter.
259.title: R

26.body: Requires glibc 2.17 or later For musl-based systems, use the linux-musl binary
26.title: Linux

260.body: SQL (Structured Query Language) : Standard language for interacting with databases. Storage Layer : Component responsible for data persistence and retrieval. Struct : Rust's custom data type for grouping related data.
260.title: S

261.body: Transaction : Sequence of database operations treated as a single unit. Trait : Rust's way of defining shared behavior (similar to interfaces). Type Safety : Guarantee that operations on data respect the data's type.
261.title: T

262.body: Unit Test : Test that verifies a small piece of code in isolation.
262.title: U

263.body: Workflow : Automated process defined in GitHub Actions for CI/CD.
263.title: W

264.body: Zero-Cost Abstraction : High-level programming constructs that compile to code as efficient as hand-written low-level code.
264.title: Z

Synapse DB consists of two main components: ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Client Application │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────┘ │ SQL Queries
┌──────────────▼──────────────────────┐
│ Query Engine │
│ • Parse SQL queries │
│ • Optimize execution plan │
│ • Execute operations │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────┘ │ Read/Write
┌──────────────▼──────────────────────┐
│ Storage Layer │
│ • Persist data to disk │
│ • Manage indexes │
│ • Handle caching │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
